chapter: Chapter I - Preliminary
title: Short title and Commencement
text:
(1) These rules may be called The Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011.
(2) They shall come into force on the 1st day of April, 2011.

chapter: Chapter I - Preliminary
title: Definitions: Act, dealer, lot

chapter: Chapter I - Preliminary
title: Definitions: manufacturer, maximum permissible error, net quantity

chapter: Chapter I - Preliminary
title: Definitions: packer, principal display panel, quantity

chapter: Chapter I - Preliminary
title: Definitions: retail dealer, retail package, retail sale, retail sale price

chapter: Chapter I - Preliminary
title: Definitions: section, Schedule, standard package, wholesale dealer, wholesale package

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Applicability of the Chapter
text:
The provisions of this Chapter shall not apply to (a) packages of commodities containing quantity of more than 25 kg or 25 litre excluding cement and fertilizer sold in bags up to 50 kg; and (b) packaged commodities meant for industrial consumers or institutional consumers.
Explanation: "institutional consumer" means the institutional consumer like transportation, Airways, Railways, Hotels, Hospitals or any other service institutions who buy packaged commodities directly from the manufacturer for use by that institution. "industrial Consumer" means the industrial consumer who buy packaged commodities directly from the manufacturer for use by that industry.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Regulation for pre-packing and sale of commodities in packaged form
text:
On and from the commencement of these rules, no person shall pre-pack or cause or permit to be pre-packed any commodity for sale, distribution or delivery unless the package in which the commodity is pre-packed bears thereon or a label is securely affixed thereto such declarations as are required to be made under these rules.
Explanation: The existence of packages without the declaration of retail sale price within the manufacturer's premises shall not be construed as a violation of these rules and it shall be ensured that all packages leaving the premises of manufacturer for their destination shall have declaration of retail sale price on them as required in these rules.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Specific commodities to be packed and sold in recommended standard packages
text:
The commodities specified in the Second Schedule shall be packed for sale, distribution or delivery in such standard quantities as are specified in that Schedule.
[Note: A prior proviso requiring a "Not a standard pack size" declaration for non-standard sizes stood withdrawn with effect from 01.07.2012 vide GSR 748(E) dated 24.10.2011.]

chapter: Chapter II - Declarations to be made on every package
title: Declaration: Manufacturer / Packer / Importer name and address
text:
Every package shall bear thereon or on the label securely affixed thereto, a definite, plain and conspicuous declaration as to: the name and address of the manufacturer, or where the manufacturer is not the packer, the name and address of the manufacturer and packer, and for any imported package the name and address of the importer shall be mentioned.
Explanation I: If any name and address of a company is mentioned on the label without any qualifying words 'manufactured by' or 'packed by', it shall be presumed that such name and address shall be that of the manufacturer and the liability shall be determined accordingly.
Explanation II: If the brand name and address of the brand owner appear on the label as a marketer, then the brand owner shall be held responsible for any violation of these rules and action shall be initiated against the deemed manufacturer; where more than one name and address appears, prosecution shall be launched against the manufacturer indicated on the label in the first place and not against all of them.
Explanation III: In respect of packages containing food articles, this sub-rule does not apply -- instead the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and rules thereunder apply.

chapter: Chapter II - Declarations to be made on every package
title: Declaration: Common/generic name of commodity
text: The common or generic names of the commodity contained in the package shall be mentioned; in case of packages with more than one product, the name and number or quantity of each product shall be mentioned on the package.

chapter: Chapter II - Declarations to be made on every package
title: Declaration: Net quantity
text: The net quantity, in terms of the standard unit of weight or measure, of the commodity contained in the package or, where the commodity is packed or sold by number, the number of the commodity contained in the package shall be mentioned.

chapter: Chapter II - Declarations to be made on every package
title: Declaration: Month and year of manufacture/pre-packing/import (date information)
text:
The month and year in which the commodity is manufactured or pre-packed or imported shall be mentioned on the package.
Provided that for packages containing food articles, the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 and rules thereunder shall apply; this sub-clause does not apply to packages containing seeds labeled and certified under the Seeds Act, 1966; and for packages containing cosmetics, the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 shall apply.
Proviso (A): No declaration as to month and year of manufacture is required on: (i) any package containing bidis or incense sticks; (ii) any domestic LPG cylinder of 14.2kg or 5kg, bottled and marketed by a public sector undertaking.
Explanation I: The month and year in which commodity is pre-packed may be expressed in words, numerals, or both.

chapter: Chapter II - Declarations to be made on every package
title: Declaration: Retail sale price (MRP)
text:
The retail sale price of the package shall be mentioned.
Provided that for packages containing alcoholic beverages or spirituous liquor, State Excise Laws apply within the State of manufacture; where State excise laws do not provide for declaration of retail sale price, these rules apply.
Proviso (C): No declaration as to retail sale price is required on: (i) any package containing bidi; (ii) any domestic LPG cylinder whose price is covered under the Administrative Price Mechanism of the Government.

chapter: Chapter II - Declarations to be made on every package
title: Declaration: Dimensions and other matters
text:
(f) Where the sizes of the commodity contained in the package are relevant, the dimensions of the commodity contained in the package shall be mentioned; if different pieces have different dimensions, the dimensions of each such different piece shall be mentioned.
(g) Such other matters as are specified in these rules.
Proviso (B): Where packaging material bearing a given month is not exhausted during that month, it may be used for pre-packing during the next succeeding month and not thereafter (subject to extension by Central Government in certain circumstances); this does not apply to food products where the 'Best before/Use before' period is ninety days or less from manufacture/packing.

chapter: Chapter II - Declarations to be made on every package
title: Declaration: Consumer care details
text: Every package shall bear the name, address, telephone number, and e-mail address (if available), of the person or office who can be contacted in case of consumer complaints.

chapter: Chapter II - Declarations to be made on every package
title: Restrictions on stickers; components sold as multiple units; use of old packaging material
text:
(3) It shall not be permissible to affix individual stickers on the package for altering or making declarations required under these rules, except that for reducing the MRP, a sticker with the revised lower MRP (inclusive of all taxes) may be affixed without covering the original MRP declaration.
(4) Stickers are permissible for declarations other than those required under these rules.
(5) Where a commodity consists of multiple components packed in two or more units for sale as a single commodity, the required declaration shall appear on the main package (with information about accompanying packages), or be given on individual packages with intimation on the main package; if sold as spare parts, all declarations shall be given on each package.
(6) Packaging material/wrapper that could not be exhausted by the manufacturer or packer may be used up to 31st March 2012 (or until exhausted, whichever is earlier), after making required corrections by stamping, sticker, or on-line printing.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Principal display panel - area, size and letter height requirements
text:
(1) For a package of capacity 5 cubic cm or less, the principal display panel may be a card or tape affixed firmly to the package bearing the required information.
(2) The height of any numeral in the declaration on the principal display panel shall not be less than the values in Table-I (net quantity by weight/volume) or Table-II (net quantity by length, area or number), as applicable.
(3) The height of letters in the declaration shall not be less than 1 mm (2 mm if blown, formed, molded, embossed or perforated); the width of a letter/numeral shall not be less than one-third of its height (except numeral '1' and letters i, I, l).
Table-I (Minimum height of numeral, net quantity by weight/volume): Up to 200g/ml -> 1mm normal / 2mm molded; Above 200g/ml to 500g/ml -> 2mm normal / 4mm molded; Above 500g/ml -> 4mm normal / 6mm molded.
Table-II (Minimum height of numeral, net quantity by length/area/number, by principal display panel area): Up to 100 cm2 -> 1mm/2mm; Above 100 to 500 cm2 -> 2mm/4mm; Above 500 to 2500 cm2 -> 4mm/6mm; Above 2500 cm2 -> 6mm/6mm.
(4) Sub-rules (1)-(3) do not apply if the information is also required under any other law in force.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Where the declaration shall appear (principal display panel placement rules)
text:
(1) Every declaration required under these rules shall appear on the principal display panel. The area surrounding the quantity declaration shall be free from printed information: (a) above and below by a space at least equal to the height of the numeral in the declaration, and (b) to the left and right by a space at least twice the height of the numeral.
(2) For soft drinks, ready-to-serve fruit beverages or similar returnable/refillable bottles, the retail sale price may be indicated on the crown cap, the bottle, or both, in the form 'MRP Rs....'.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Manner in which declarations shall be made (legibility, contrast, language)
text:
(1) Every declaration shall be (a) legible and prominent; (b) numerals of retail sale price and net quantity shall be printed, painted or inscribed in a colour that contrasts conspicuously with the label background -- except where information is blown/formed/molded on glass or plastic (contrasting colour not required), and hand-written/hand-script declarations must be clear, unambiguous and legible.
(2) No declaration shall require reading through any liquid commodity in the package.
(3) Where a package has an outside container/wrapper, that container/wrapper shall also bear all required declarations, except where it is transparent and the underlying declarations are easily readable through it, or where the inner package itself bears no declaration on its outer cover.
(4) Declarations shall be in Hindi (Devanagari script) or English; other languages may additionally be used.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Declaration of name and address of the manufacturer/packer/importer - detailed requirements
text:
(1) Every package kept, offered, exposed for sale or sold shall bear conspicuously the name and complete address of the manufacturer, or where the manufacturer is not the packer, of both manufacturer and packer, and for imported packages, the name and address of the importer.
Proviso: For packages of capacity 5 cubic cm or less, a mark or inscription enabling identification of the manufacturer/packer/importer suffices. Where a commodity manufactured outside India is packed in India, the principal display panel shall also show the name and complete address of the Indian packer/importer.
Explanation: "complete address" means the postal address of the factory, or the street name, premises number (if any), and either the city/State or PIN code, sufficient for a consumer to identify and locate the manufacturer/packer/importer.
(2) The name of the manufacturer/packer/importer shall be the actual corporate name, or if not incorporated, the name under which the business is conducted in India.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: General provisions relating to declaration of quantity
text:
(1) In declaring net quantity, the weight of wrappers and materials other than the commodity shall be excluded.
(2) Where a commodity is not likely to vary in weight/measure due to environmental conditions, the declared quantity shall correspond to what the consumer actually receives, and shall not be qualified by 'when packed' or similar words.
(3) Where variation due to environmental conditions is likely but negligible, the declared quantity shall account for such variation so the consumer receives not less than the declared quantity, and shall not be qualified by 'when packed'.
(4) Declarations for commodities likely to undergo significant environmental variation may be qualified by 'when packed', as specified in the Third Schedule.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Manner in which declaration of quantity shall be made
text:
(1) Quantity shall be expressed in a unit of weight, measure, number, or combination that gives accurate and adequate information to the consumer.
(2) Except for commodities in the Fourth Schedule, quantity shall be declared in terms of: (a) mass for solid/semi-solid/viscous/mixed commodities; (b) length for linear-measure goods; (c) area for area-measure goods; (d) volume for liquid/cubic-measure goods; (e) number for goods sold by number.
(3) Where quantity is declared by mass, an additional declaration of number of commodities in the package may optionally be made.
(4) Where weight/measure/number declaration alone is insufficient, it shall be accompanied by a declaration of dimensions and/or number as necessary.
(5) Additional information necessary for the consumer shall appear on the same panel as other required information.
(6) The declaration of quantity shall not contain words or expressions creating an exaggerated, misleading or inadequate impression of quantity -- e.g. 'minimum', 'not less than', 'average', 'about', 'approximately', or similar.
(7) For packages of capacity 5 cubic cm or less, the quantity declaration shall be on a tag/card/tape/device affixed such that it cannot be removed without opening the container, and shall bear a mark enabling identification of the manufacturer/packer.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Statement of units of weight, measure or number
text:
(2) For quantities less than one kilogram/metre/sq.metre/cubic metre/cubic decimetre/litre, the unit shall be gram/centimetre/sq.decimetre/cubic centimetre/cubic centimetre/millilitre respectively.
(3) For quantities equal to or more than those units, the larger unit shall be used with fractions expressed in decimal sub-multiples (subject to an option to express certain round quantities in the smaller unit).
(4) No number called dozen, score, gross, great gross or the like shall be specified on any package.
(5) Only the International System of Units (SI) shall be used for net quantity; items sold by number shall use symbol 'N' or 'U'.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Declarations with regard to dimensions of certain commodities (textiles etc.)
text: Where a package contains commodities like bed-sheets, hemmed fabric materials, dhoties, sarees, napkins, pillow-covers, towels, table cloths or similar, the number and finished-size dimensions of such commodities shall be declared on the package or label. If the package contains pieces of different dimensions, the package shall declare the dimensions and retail sale price of each piece, and these shall also be marked on each individual piece.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Declaration with regard to dimensions and weight where these relate to price
text: Where the dimensions and/or weight of a commodity has a relationship to its price, the declaration of quantity on the package shall also include a declaration of such dimensions, weight, or combination thereof.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Declaration of number of usable sheets
text: For packages containing sheets such as aluminum foil, facial tissues, waxed paper, toilet paper or similar, the quantity declaration shall include the number of usable sheets and the dimensions of each sheet.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Declarations with regard to dimensions of container-type commodities
text: For commodities like bags, boxes, cups, pans etc. sold as containers: (i) bag-type: number of bags plus linear dimensions; (ii) square/oblong/rectangular containers: number of containers plus length, width, and depth if required; (iii) circular/round containers: number of items plus diameter and depth if necessary; (iv) where container capacity is referenced by standard weight/measure, that reference shall be included in the quantity declaration.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Provisions relating to wholesale and retail dealers (sale price compliance, revised prices, weighing machines)
text:
(1) No wholesale/retail dealer or importer shall sell, distribute, deliver, display or store any packaged commodity unless it complies fully with the Act and these rules.
(2) No dealer shall sell packaged commodities at a price exceeding the declared retail sale price.
(3) Where tax on a pre-packed commodity is revised after packing, retail sale shall not exceed the revised price communicated by the manufacturer/packer via newspaper advertisements and notices to dealers and Legal Metrology authorities, subject to specified limits and procedures; lower revised prices must be honoured immediately.
(5) No dealer shall obliterate, smudge or alter the retail sale price on a package or label.
(6) The manufacturer/packer/importer shall not alter the price on wrapper material once printed and used.
(7) Retailers covered under VAT/TOT dealing in commodities declared by weight/volume shall maintain an accuracy-class-III electronic weighing machine with printed receipt facility, free for consumer use, at a prominent place in their premises.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Inspection of quantity and error at manufacturer's or packer's premises
text: Authorized Legal Metrology Officers may examine packages and carry out tests at the manufacturer's or packer's premises, drawing samples per the Fifth Schedule and testing per the Sixth Schedule. Results are recorded on the Form in the Seventh Schedule, signed by the manufacturer/packer or a witness. A lot is approved for sale only if: (a) the statistical average net quantity of sample packages is equal to or more than the declared quantity; (b) the error in deficiency in no sample exceeds the maximum permissible error; and (c) each package bears all required declarations. Non-compliant lots may require 100% check and re-packing/re-labeling/re-processing before sale. For non-compliance, five representative samples may be seized as evidence.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Action on completion of inspection at manufacturer/packer premises
text: If the inspection report shows the statistical average net quantity is less than declared, or error in deficiency exceeds the maximum permissible error, or required declarations are missing, the Legal Metrology Officer shall seize the sample packages for safe custody as evidence and initiate action for violations under the Act and rules, subject to the fresh-testing provisions of Rule 19(4). Disposal of seized packages follows the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Inspection of quantity and error at premises of wholesale or retail dealer
text: Tests at a dealer's premises are ordinarily conducted only on complaint, suspicion of tampering/pilferage/leakage, or where required declarations are missing. If error in deficiency exceeds the maximum permissible error, the officer shall seize the package and take action against the dealer, except where the package bears 'when packed' and the deficiency is shown to be due to environmental conditions. If declarations are missing, the officer may enquire into the source of the package.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Establishment of maximum permissible error on package
text:
(1) The maximum permissible error for commodities shall be as specified in the First Schedule.
(2) In establishing it, account is taken of: (a) unavoidable deviation in weighing/measuring/counting under good packaging practice; (b) variation from ordinary/customary exposure to climate, transport, storage etc. under good distribution practice; (c) variation due to nature of packaging material or container.
(3) For commodities qualified by 'when packed', the Director/Controller/Legal Metrology Officer determines the reasonable variation attributable to environmental conditions.

chapter: Chapter II - Provisions Applicable to Retail Sale Packages
title: Deceptive packages to be repacked or seized
text: Where the quantity in a sample package agrees with its declaration but the package is 'deceptive' (designed to give an exaggerated/misleading impression of quantity, unless bigger dimensions are justified for product protection or filling-machine requirements), the officer shall require the manufacturer/packer to repack and re-label it; failure results in seizure and punitive action, with safe custody of packages as evidence. Perishable seized commodities are disposed of per rules under the Act.

chapter: Chapter III - Wholesale Packages
title: Declarations applicable on every wholesale package
text: Every wholesale package shall bear a legible, definite, plain and conspicuous declaration as to: (a) name and address of the manufacturer or importer, or the packer if different; (b) identity of the commodity; and (c) total number of retail packages contained, or the net quantity in standard units, of the commodity in the wholesale package. This rule does not apply where a similar declaration is already required by other law.

chapter: Chapter IV - Export and Import of Packaged Commodities
title: Restrictions on sale of export packages in India
text: An export package shall not be sold in India unless the manufacturer or packer has re-packed or re-labeled the commodity in accordance with Chapter II. Non-compliant export packages sold in India are liable to seizure under the Act.

chapter: Chapter V - Exemptions
title: Exemption in respect of certain packages
text: These rules do not apply to any package containing a commodity if: (a) the net weight/measure is 10g/10ml or less, if sold by weight/measure (though MRP and net quantity must still be declared for packages of 10g-20g or 10ml-20ml); (b) it is a fast food item packed by a restaurant/hotel and the like; (c) it contains scheduled/non-scheduled formulations under the Drugs (Price Control) Order, 1995; (d) it is an agricultural farm produce package above 50 kg.

chapter: Chapter VI - Registration of Manufacturers and Packers
title: Registration of manufacturers, packers and importers
text: Every person/firm/entity that pre-packs or imports any commodity for sale must apply for registration of name and address to the Director/Controller with a fee of Rs.500, within ninety days of commencement of pre-packing/import activity (or of these rules, if already active). The application must state the applicant's name, complete address of the pre-packing/import premises, and the commodity/commodities involved. Alteration of the registration certificate requires a fee of Rs.100. The Registering Authority must return incomplete applications within 7 working days, or register and grant a certificate if complete.

chapter: Chapter VI - Registration of Manufacturers and Packers
title: Registration of shorter address
text: A manufacturer or packer may apply to register a shorter address in addition to the complete address. The Director/Controller may register it if satisfied it is sufficient for identification. Once registered, the shorter address may be used on labels.

chapter: Chapter VI - Registration of Manufacturers and Packers
title: Maintenance and circulation of the registration list
text:
Rule 29: The Director/Controller shall maintain a register of the name and complete address of each registered manufacturer/packer, open to public inspection free of charge.
Rule 30: The Director/Controller shall compile a State-wise list of registered manufacturers/packers and circulate it to the concerned State Controller to enable sampling at manufacturer/packer premises.

chapter: Chapter VII - General
title: Advertisements mentioning retail sale price
text:
(1) Any advertisement mentioning the retail sale price of a pre-packaged commodity shall also declare the net quantity or number of the commodity in the package.
(2) The font size of the net quantity declaration in the advertisement shall match that of the retail sale price.

chapter: Chapter VII - General
title: Penalty for contravention of Rules
text:
(1) Contravention of Rules 27 to 31 (registration and advertisement provisions) is punishable with a fine of four thousand rupees.
(2) Contravention of any other provision of these rules, for which no punishment is otherwise provided, is punishable with a fine of two thousand rupees.

chapter: Chapter VII - General
title: Power to relax
text: The Central Government may, after verifying the genuineness of a compounding of a case or Court decision, permit a manufacturer or packer to pack for sale for a reasonable period by relaxing one or more provisions of these rules, subject to specified corrective measures.

chapter: Chapter VII - General
title: Repeal and savings
text: The Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 1977 are repealed, without affecting prior operations, accrued rights/liabilities, penalties, or pending investigations/proceedings under the old rules, which continue as if the old rules had not been rescinded. Registrations, licenses, approvals, and pending applications under the old rules continue in force under the corresponding provisions of these rules.

chapter: Schedules
title: Maximum permissible errors on net quantity declared by weight or volume
text:
Declared quantity (g or ml) -> Maximum permissible error (% or g/ml): Up to 50 -> 9% ; 50-100 -> 4.5 g/ml; 100-200 -> 4.5%; 200-300 -> 9 g/ml; 300-500 -> 3%; 500-1000 -> 15 g/ml; 1000-10000 -> 1.5%; 10000-15000 -> 150 g/ml; More than 15000 -> 1.0%.
The percentage-based error is rounded to the nearest one-tenth of a g/ml for declared quantities up to 1000 g/ml, and to the next whole g/ml above 1000 g/ml.

chapter: Schedules
title: Maximum permissible errors on net quantity declared by length, area or number
text:
Length: 2% of declared quantity up to 10 metre, thereafter 1%.
Area: 4% of declared quantity up to 10 sq. metre, thereafter 1%.
Number: 2% of declared quantity.

chapter: Schedules
title: Commodities to be packed in specified standard quantities
text:
Lists mandatory standard pack sizes for specific commodities including: Baby food/weaning food (100g-10kg in listed steps); Biscuits (25g-1kg in listed steps); Bread (multiples of 100g); Butter/margarine (25g-5kg+ in listed steps); Cereals and pulses (100g-5kg+); Coffee (25g-1kg+); Tea (25g-1kg+); Beverage-reconstitution materials (25g-1kg+); Edible oils/vanaspati/ghee/butter oil (50g-5kg+); Milk powder (50g-500g+); Non-soapy detergent powder (50g-1kg+); Rice/flour/atta/rawa/suji (100g-5kg+); Salt (10g-5kg+); Soaps -- laundry (50g+), non-soapy detergent cakes (50g-100g+), toilet soap (25g-50g+); Aerated soft drinks/non-alcoholic beverages (65ml-5 litre); Mineral/drinking water (100ml-5 litre); Cement in bags (1kg-50kg); Paint/varnish/enamel (50ml-5 litre+), paste/solid paint (500g-5kg+), base paint (450ml-4 litre).
[Exact step values for each commodity are in the source Second Schedule table and should be consulted directly for precise compliance checks.]

chapter: Schedules
title: Commodities whose quantity declaration may be qualified by 'When packed'
text: 1. All kinds of Soaps. 2. Lotions. 3. Cream (other than cream of milk).

chapter: Schedules
title: Exceptions to standard unit-of-measure rules (Rule 12(2))
text: Lists commodities permitted to declare quantity in a specified unit other than the default rule, e.g.: Aerosol products (weight); Acids in liquid form (weight or volume); Compressed/liquefied gas other than LPG (weight and equivalent volume); Curd (weight); Electric cables/wire (length or weight); Fencing wire (number or weight); Fruits (number or weight); Furnace oil, non-edible vegetable oil, edible oil/vanaspati/ghee/butter oil (weight or volume); Heavy residual fuel oil (weight); Industrial diesel fuel (volume); Honey/malt-extract/golden syrup/treacle (weight); Ice cream and similar frozen products (weight, per 2012 amendment); Liquid chemicals (weight or volume); LPG (weight); Nails/wood screws (number or weight); Paints/varnish/enamels other than paste/solid (volume); Paste/solid paint (weight); Rasgulla/Gulabjamun and sweet preparations (weight); Ready-made garments (number); Sauces (weight); Tyres and tubes (number); Yarn (weight or length); Cosmetics including creams/shampoo/lotions/perfumes (weight or measure).

chapter: Schedules
title: Manner of selection of sample packages for testing
text: Sample size by lot size: Lot size less than 4000 -> sample size 32; lot size more than 4000 -> sample size 80. Samples must be selected at random, representatively spread across the stock (top, bottom, center, sides, front, rear) or introduced at random into the packing/filling process as specified.

chapter: Schedules
title: Determination of the net quantity of commodities in packages (testing methodology)
text: Specifies the equipment, working standards, and step-by-step procedures Legal Metrology Officers must use to determine tare weight, gross weight, and net quantity of sampled packages (by weight, volume/liquid content, length, or number), including procedures for destructive testing via empty-package sampling, and requirements for recording results on the Form in the Seventh Schedule. Also covers checking of other declarations for conformity and adequacy under Rule 6(1)(g)-(h).

chapter: Schedules
title: Inspection data-sheet forms (Form A: weight checking; Form B: volume/length checking)
text: Prescribes the standard data-sheet forms used by Legal Metrology Officers to record: package particulars (manufacturer/packer name, address, price, month/year), commodity classification (lot size, sample size, applicable Schedule/Class, maximum permissible error %), sample-by-sample weight/volume/length checking data with remarks/errors, declared vs. average results, general compliance comments, and signatures of the authorized officer, manufacturer/packer (or witness), with place, designation, name and time.
